Let’s talk about something that holds so many of us back: perfectionism.
Welcome to Chapter 5, Progress Over Perfection: The Power of Starting Before Feeling Ready.
Have you ever found yourself stuck, endlessly planning or overthinking because you wanted everything to be just right before taking the first step? You’re definitely not alone.
The truth is, chasing perfection can actually freeze us in place. We start second-guessing every move, worried about making mistakes, or what others might think if we fall short. That fear can be so strong, it keeps us from ever really getting started.
But here’s the thing—real progress comes when you let go of perfect and just start moving forward. It’s all about valuing action and learning, instead of flawless performance. The people who go the farthest are usually the ones who are willing to begin, even when things aren’t ideal.
Perfectionism tricks us into thinking there’s a perfect time to begin, or that we’ll be ready if we just prepare a little longer. But most learning happens while we’re actually doing the thing, not just thinking about it. Mistakes? They’re going to happen. But they’re also what help us grow.
So, how do you break free from perfectionism and start making real progress? Try these practical steps:
First, set a clear but flexible goal. Know what you want to achieve, but give yourself permission to adjust as you go and learn.
Next, look for the smallest possible step you can take right now—even if it feels tiny. That first bit of action counts for so much.
And finally, celebrate the effort, not just the end result. Just getting started takes courage, and that’s worth recognizing.
This whole approach matters even more if you’re working on something creative or entrepreneurial—those projects where uncertainty is just part of the deal. If you wait for conditions to be perfect, you might end up waiting forever. The folks who succeed? They’re the ones who step forward before they feel completely ready, and learn as they go.
Think about an aspiring writer who commits to writing just one page a day, instead of waiting for the perfect idea or the perfect mood. Day by day, they actually build a body of work. Or picture an entrepreneur who puts out a simple version of their product to get real feedback, rather than spending years trying to perfect it in secret. They learn so much faster, just by taking action.
The real magic happens when you treat every step as an experiment, not a final verdict. This mindset helps take the fear out of failing and encourages you to keep learning. Over time, those small actions add up, and before you know it, you’re making serious progress.
So here’s the key takeaway: When you focus on progress instead of perfection, you unlock real momentum. You stop worrying so much about what could go wrong, and start discovering all the things you can learn and accomplish with steady effort. By giving yourself permission to start—even when you don’t feel totally ready—you make the path forward so much clearer and, honestly, a lot more rewarding.
